Methods that skip access checks on private properties

Methods named with __ that PHP calls at lifecycle points
questions.x: Magic methods always start with a double underscore. PHP invokes them automatically at points in an object life, such as creation, destruction, deserialization, or string conversion. You do not call them yourself.
questions.h: The names start with __. Who actually invokes them, your code or PHP?

questions.q: When does PHP call __construct() on an object?
o: When the object is deserialized from a cookie string
When the object is created with new ClassName() in code
When the object goes out of scope at the end of a request
When the object is used in echo or string concatenation
questions.x: __construct() runs when an object is created with new. It does not run on unserialize(). Deserialization is a different lifecycle event, handled by __wakeup() instead.
questions.h: Which PHP syntax is the normal way to create a brand-new object?

questions.q: When does PHP call __destruct() on an object?
o: When the object is destroyed, such as at script end
When your code calls delete() on the object by name
When unserialize() first finishes rebuilding the object
When the object is compared to a string with ===
questions.x: __destruct() runs when the object is destroyed: it goes out of scope, the script ends, or it is garbage collected. After a request that deserialized a cookie object, PHP destroys that object and __destruct() fires on its own.
questions.h: The attacker never calls this method. When does PHP destroy objects created during a request?

questions.q: When does PHP call __wakeup() on an object?
o: When the object is first created with the new keyword
When the PHP session is closed and written to disk
When the object is deserialized with unserialize()
When the object is converted to a string for output
questions.x: __wakeup() runs when an object is deserialized. That is the unserialize() path, not new. __toString() is the method that runs when the object is treated as a string.
questions.h: The object was stored as a string. Which magic method runs as that string becomes an object again?

questions.q: Why is __destruct() useful to an attacker who can unserialize a cookie?
o: It bypasses PHP type checks so any property can call any function
PHP calls it automatically when the object is later destroyed
It is the only magic method allowed to read files from disk
It runs before __construct(), so authentication has not started
questions.x: Deserializing a cookie creates the object in memory. When the request finishes, PHP destroys it and __destruct() runs without any explicit call. The attacker only needs to supply the serialized object.
questions.h: The attacker controls the cookie, not the call stack. Which method still runs when the request ends?
